hypothesis: Writer identity may be represented more consistently across scripts as deviation from the script-specific population center than as the raw embedding itself.
useful_auc_gain: script-relative minus raw cross-script macro AUC >= 0.01
strong_auc_gain: script-relative minus raw cross-script macro AUC >= 0.03
useful_eer_reduction: script-relative pooled EER decreases by at least 0.01 absolute

interpretation_cases.strong_support: At least one encoder gains >= 0.03 macro AUC, with no material EER degradation.
interpretation_cases.promising_support: At least one encoder gains >= 0.01 macro AUC but less than 0.03.
interpretation_cases.no_support: Both encoders gain less than 0.01 macro AUC.
interpretation_cases.harmful: Script-relative transformation decreases macro AUC for both encoders.

novelty_interpretation.helps_both_encoders: Script-relative representation may be a general cross-script verification principle.
novelty_interpretation.helps_wgc_more: Script-relative representation may interact productively with geometry consistency.
novelty_interpretation.removes_wgc_advantage: The script-relative transformation may explain part of the effect previously attributed to WGC.
